stages.label: legacy-before-authorship
stages.explanation: A proposal, formal review and editorial opinion exist before authorship activation.

stages.label: activated-generation-two
stages.explanation: One-way activation advances policy generation and does not backfill old authorship.

stages.label: identity-and-role-enforced
stages.explanation: Claims require a current local grant, its exact principal and its author role.

stages.label: authenticated-worker-queue
stages.explanation: Three jobs create immutable grant-bound proofs for two registered author principals.

stages.label: exact-scope-and-rollback
stages.explanation: Out-of-scope submission rolls back the candidate and proof; the original grant can extend its own lease.

stages.label: regrant-and-fenced-reclaim
stages.explanation: A replacement grant cannot continue or relabel an old attempt; a fresh fenced attempt succeeds and old proofs remain inspectable.

stages.label: compose-after-author-revocation
stages.explanation: Historical author authorization remains valid when a later integrator composes the exact original components.

stages.label: nested-transitive-provenance
stages.explanation: The root pins a four-proposal ancestry and all four contributors, including the intermediate integrator.

stages.label: unproven-component-rejected
stages.explanation: Composition requires an existing valid proof for every direct and transitive source.

stages.label: contributors-separated-globally
stages.explanation: New role grants cannot let source authors or intermediate integrators review the root; exclusion covers every write and verdict.

stages.label: contributor-coordinator-blocked
stages.explanation: A separate coordinator grant for an intermediate integrator remains excluded; an unrelated coordinator still needs formal review and every editorial quorum.

stages.label: formal-review-and-first-reviewer
stages.explanation: A valid formal review and one reviewer per write cannot meet the two-principal policy.

stages.label: current-approvals-observed
stages.explanation: Two noncontributor principal IDs approve each write under generation 2; the observation does not itself accept the root.

stages.label: accepted-with-provenance-receipt
stages.explanation: Atomic acceptance checks runtime guards, formal review, current local authority, noncontributor quorums and exact authorship; the receipt pins the proof.

stages.label: completed-replays-preserve-proof
stages.explanation: Current original integrator authority can replay a completed composition despite stale source reads; coordinator replay returns the original receipt without new events.

stages.label: historical-proofs-and-runtime-guards
stages.explanation: Legacy proposals receive no retroactive proof; a proven and approved competing proposal still cannot override stale_read.

limitations: The SQLite owner and local clock are trusted; local digests do not provide external attestation.
A bearer credential proves possession of a local grant, not a person's identity, SSO, model identity or expertise.
Different registered principal IDs do not establish independent people, models, organizations or evidence.
The proof records authority at submission and exact component ancestry; it does not prove how the text was created.
Legacy proposals receive no backfilled proof; activation also advances the editorial policy generation.
Historical proofs survive later grant revocation, while protected mutation and replay require the current original grant.
All reviews and decisions are programmed local examples, with no human review or external LLM call.
The code is stored data and may be parsed by formal guards; it is never executed by this workflow.
Contributor separation is global to the candidate, not limited to the files personally written by a contributor.
Authority, provenance and voting do not establish prose truth, code behavior, semantic completeness or external publication permission.
Sequential public snapshots are observations; Store.accept is the transaction boundary for new acceptance.
Configured Python workers are not a measurement of throughput, supported agent count or LLM capacity.
Credentials, credential hashes and SQLite stay private; no release or Git publication is created by this command.
